clue.text: Princess has aged no end

parts.note: someone who has aged is older, so has stands for is here

indicators.note: with no end, the final letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: aged means grown older

explanation.surface: A royal daughter is said to be getting on in years, without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' drops the final R; read 'has aged' as 'is older'.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the Irish princess of the Tristan legend and Wagner's opera.

clue.text: Wanting wood mite burned, unfortunately

indicators.note: things going unfortunately go awry, so the letters of these two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A house lacking timber because an insect was sadly incinerated.
explanation.definitionFit: Untimbered means lacking timber, so a structure built without any woodwork.

clue.text: Loss of guts from fish biting large parts of line

indicators.note: biting means the fish holds the next letter in its mouth, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: cod is a fish
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
metrical feet are the units that make up a line of verse

explanation.surface: An angler loses nerve as a fish bites on most of the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'biting' signals the container; the line is a line of verse, whose metrical units are feet, not fishing line.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting cold feet is the idiom for losing one's nerve, so courage or guts deserting someone.

clue.text: Musician's time to follow sextet again

indicators.note: to follow means this piece comes after the others in the answer

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
bis is the musical direction to repeat, meaning twice or again

explanation.surface: A player's tempo comes after a group of six play the piece once more.
explanation.definitionFit: A vibist is a vibraphone player, so a performer on that instrument.

clue.text: Evil at heart, become bad and spiteful

indicators.note: at heart takes the central letters of the word Evil

parts.note: food that perishes goes off, so becomes bad

explanation.surface: Someone wicked deep down turns rotten and nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Viperish describes venomous, malicious behaviour like that attributed to a snake.

clue.text: British feller's posters

parts.note: a feller of trees is a logger; feller's here stands for the plural, fellers

explanation.surface: Billboards belonging to a British chap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feller' looks like slang for a fellow but is one who fells trees; posters are people who post online.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloggers are people who post entries on the internet, so they are posters.

clue.text: Stripping off, assistant crime-fighter breaks gun out

indicators.note: breaks means the sidekick splits the other letters apart, sitting inside them
out signals that the letters of gun are put out of order

parts.note: Robin is Batman's assistant in fighting crime

explanation.surface: Batman's sidekick undresses after a weapon goes missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the three letters into UNG, and 'breaks' splits them around the sidekick's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrobing means taking off one's robes or clothes, so undressing.

clue.text: Trump, scratching bottom, is a terrible fellow

indicators.note: scratching out the bottom of a down answer removes its final letter

parts.note: Ivana Trump was Donald Trump's first wife

explanation.surface: A former US president, a rear-end scratcher, is called an awful man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratching bottom' drops the last A of IVANA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan the Terrible was the sixteenth-century tsar of Russia, a fellow with that epithet.

clue.text: Errand boy not following viable plan

indicators.note: not means the following letter is taken away

parts.note: a gofer is someone who runs errands
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A messenger boy refuses to go along with a workable scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A goer is informally a proposal that will work, a project that will go ahead.

clue.text: What stalker does for walks, oddly

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: oddly takes the letters in odd positions of the word walks

explanation.surface: Describes a stalker's activity as one of going on walks, strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalker moves stealthily around looking for prey, which is to prowl.

clue.text: Time (100 years) in enclosure like each other across answer?

definitions.text: enclosure like each other across answer?

parts.note: bird is slang for a prison sentence, time inside
C is the Roman numeral for 100
an age is a span of many years

explanation.surface: A spell of a century spent inside a pen, like the rest of the grid's answers.
explanation.walkthrough: Every other across answer hides a bird: IBIS, ROBIN, OWL, EGRET, ROC, TIT, ERNE, EMU, SWAN, LARK and so on, so each is a cage for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A birdcage holds a bird, as each other across answer contains one inside it.

clue.text: Lager better in a cocktail? It's too bad

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Mixing beer into a cocktail is called a crying shame.
explanation.definitionFit: Something regrettable is unfortunate and to be deplored, so a pity.

clue.text: Shades including black on woodcut

indicators.note: on means the wood comes next, placed after the shades in this down answer
including means the colours hold the next letter inside

parts.note: tones are shades of colour
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
teak is a wood; the word also contains cut, which does double duty as the definition of a cut of meat

explanation.surface: Colours, black among them, laid onto a woodcut print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woodcut' splits into wood, the hardwood, and cut, the definition: a cut of meat. 'including' puts B after the T of the shades.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-bone steak is a cut of beef containing a T-shaped bone.

clue.text: Harder pork pie consumed by pilot

indicators.note: consumed by means the lie goes inside the other word

parts.note: to pilot is to steer
pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for lie

explanation.surface: A pilot eats a tougher pork pie.
explanation.walkthrough: PORKY PIE or PORK PIE is British rhyming slang for a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Steelier means more like steel, so tougher or harder.

clue.text: Each French writer holding universal sway

parts.note: per means each, as in so much per head

indicators.note: holding means the writer contains the letter inside

parts.note: the Marquis de Sade was a French writer
U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: A French author with universal appeal wields influence over each reader.
explanation.definitionFit: To persuade is to bring someone round by argument, to influence them.

clue.text: Address to superior officer going back and forth in wind

parts.note: sir is how one addresses a superior officer

indicators.note: going back means the letters run backwards, then forth means they run forwards again

parts.note: CO, commanding officer, read once back and once forth

explanation.surface: Saluting a senior officer while pacing up and down in a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: The superior officer is also a CO (commanding officer), read 'going back' as OC and then 'forth' as CO.
explanation.definitionFit: The sirocco is a hot dust-laden wind blowing from North Africa into southern Europe.

clue.text: Setter gasping a small feature of Windows

indicators.note: gasping means the setter takes in air, here taking in the other letters

parts.note: cement is something that sets

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler panting at a minor aspect of a computer system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the compiler; it is cement, which sets. Windows is capitalised to suggest software.
explanation.definitionFit: A casement is a hinged window that opens like a door, a kind of window feature.

clue.text: Name again protected by secret? It leaks

indicators.note: protected by means the answer is held within the following words

explanation.surface: A name covered by confidentiality is being leaked.
explanation.definitionFit: To retitle something is to give it a new title, to rename it.

clue.text: Thin quality of cape put on head of Swiss bank?

indicators.note: put on means the cape is added on after the other letters
head of takes the first letter of the word Swiss

parts.note: a bank is a lender of money
a ness is a headland or cape

explanation.surface: A slim cloak worn by a Swiss bank's chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Slenderness is the state of being slim, the property of thinness.

clue.text: Swallowing tablet, recover in truth

indicators.note: swallowing means the word for recover takes the pill inside

parts.note: to rally is to recover strength
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: A patient takes a pill and gets better, truly.
explanation.definitionFit: Really means actually or genuinely, the same as in truth.

clue.text: Desperate disheartened Madame Bovary?

indicators.note: desperate signals that the remaining letters are thrown into wild disorder
disheartened removes the heart, the two middle letters, of the word Madame

explanation.surface: Flaubert's despairing heroine, Madame Bovary, is crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' takes DA from MADAME to leave MAME, and 'Desperate' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is the first name of Flaubert's heroine Madame Bovary.

clue.text: After opening of bottle, down coke in New York

indicators.note: After means the next piece follows the first letter
opening of takes the first letter of the word bottle

parts.note: low means down, as in feeling low

explanation.surface: Having uncorked a bottle, someone downs a cola in Manhattan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coke' looks like the drink; in US slang blow is cocaine.
explanation.definitionFit: Blow is American slang for cocaine, the drug often called coke.

clue.text: Alaskan often on the pull is quiet after sex

indicators.note: after means the quiet word comes behind the other

parts.note: male is one of the sexes
mute means silent or quiet

explanation.surface: An Alaskan out on the pull goes quiet after sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the pull' suggests flirting; the malamute or malemute is a sled dog that pulls sledges.
explanation.definitionFit: The malemute is a large Alaskan sledge dog bred for hauling loads.

clue.text: Guy backing fighter where he had a thrilling fight?

definitions.text: where he had a thrilling fight?

parts.note: a guy is a man

indicators.note: backing means the fighter's name is read backwards

parts.note: Muhammad Ali was a boxer

explanation.surface: A man supporting a boxer at the venue of a great bout.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1975 Ali–Frazier fight was billed the Thrilla in Manila; 'he' refers back to the fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: Manila, capital of the Philippines, hosted Ali's famous 'Thrilla in Manila' boxing match.

clue.text: River feature, one parent of ugly ducklings?

parts.note: a means one
the ugly duckling of the fairy tale is a cygnet, whose mother, or dam, is a swan

explanation.surface: A mother of ugly ducklings found on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Aswan Dam is on the Nile in Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aswan Dam is a huge structure across the Nile, a river feature in Egypt.

clue.text: Sci-fi writer's bit of exaltation in religious group

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
an exaltation is the collective noun for larks, so one lark is a bit of one

explanation.surface: A science-fiction author's moment of rapture within a church congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur C. Clarke wrote 2001: A Space Odyssey and other science fiction.
